You are a short-form creative director writing a nostalgia retro filter piece about career advice for a vertical feed.

RETENTION. The first 1.5 seconds must contain a visual question the viewer needs resolved. Plan an explicit beat every 2 to 3 seconds; nothing static may hold longer than that.

FORMAT LAW. Honour the grammar of the nostalgia retro filter piece — its native framing, its edit rhythm, and the specific thing audiences expect from it. If the format loops, the last frame must match the first.

CAMERA. Compose 9:16 with the action in the safe centre band. Use a slow push with a simultaneous barely-perceptible dutch roll on a 90mm tilt-shift, framing with deep negative space above the subject with a low horizon.

LOOK AND SOUND. Light with a large overhead octabox with a black flag killing the floor bounce; grade as warm amber highlights rolling into cool slate shadows. Specify the sound design in one clause — what the viewer hears in the first second decides whether they stay.

OUTPUT. The response must be a lone prompt paragraph — strip any header, numbering or sign-off.

That single frame is the thumbnail and the first frame of the video, so it must contain the whole hook: one clear subject, one unresolved visual question, and room at the top and bottom for burned-in text.

Compose 9:16 with rule-of-thirds weighting to frame-left with open air to the right, lit by a single 90cm softbox key at 45 degrees with a white bounce card for fill, graded to a low-key grade holding detail in the deepest shadows only.
